name: profile-close-window-light
prompt: Tall portrait photograph, tight head-and-shoulders close-up taken with an 85mm portrait lens wide open at f/1.8, the focus pinned on the knit. A single person turns their left cheek toward the lens at a three-quarter angle, chin raised, neck craned back, gazing upward at something vast. Their head is sealed inside a charcoal hand-knit balaclava of thick ribbed wool, a completely blank knitted surface with no openings for eyes, nose or mouth. A thick white yarn circle is stitched as a border tracing the edge of the face, and inside that circle, up near its rim at roughly two o'clock and sitting above the left eye, the eye nearest the camera, is a red felt triangle with rounded corners, clearly placed off-centre and high rather than in the middle. The knit tucks neatly under the turned-up cord collar of a present-day olive waxed jacket; a black knitted glove grips that collar, the jacket sleeve hanging past the wrist so not one patch of skin is visible. Low golden sunlight slants in from a window just out of shot at about forty-five degrees, grazing the wool so each rib and stray fibre throws a tiny shadow and glows honey-amber, while the opposite cheek drops into soft dusk shade. Above and behind, melting into creamy bokeh, climbs a cliff of stacked paper reams and string-tied bundles in chilly blue-white, crowding the top half of the image; one sheet near the line of the gaze carries a black printed heading, THE RULES, just legible through the blur. Warm amber on charcoal wool set against cool paper white, gentle grain, an ordinary British flat on a weekday afternoon, real cloth, real paper, nothing metal or glowing.
